content: Voglibose, known by its International Nonproprietary Name (INN) and United States Adopted Name (USAN), is a pharmaceutical agent classified as an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor. It is specifically utilized to reduce postprandial blood glucose levels in individuals diagnosed with diabetes mellitus. This medication is manufactured in India by Ranbaxy Laboratories and is marketed under the trade name Volix. Additionally, Glenmark Pharmaceuticals produces voglibose under the brand name Vocarb. Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia, which arises due to either a relative or absolute deficiency of insulin or the presence of insulin resistance. Postprandial hyperglycemia (PPHG) refers to elevated blood glucose levels following a meal, primarily caused by impaired first-phase insulin secretion. Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors, such as voglibose, function by delaying the absorption of glucose in the intestines, thereby preventing a rapid post-meal surge in blood glucose levels. There are three primary molecules within the alpha-glucosidase inhibitor class: acarbose, miglitol, and voglibose. Among these, voglibose is the most recent addition to the class. It demonstrates superior efficacy and a more favorable side effect profile compared to both acarbose and miglitol. Numerous clinical trials have validated the effectiveness of voglibose in managing postprandial hyperglycemia. It is important to note that postprandial hyperglycemia, rather than fasting plasma glucose (FPG), has been identified as a significant marker for cardiovascular disorders associated with diabetes. Therefore, controlling PPHG is critical in the comprehensive management of diabetes. Voglibose is specifically indicated for the management of PPHG and is available in a 0.3 mg dosage under the brand name VOLIBO.
